summary_html: Family agrees to a **voluntary service plan**—counseling, substance-use treatment, parenting classes—designed to correct conditions without court compulsion. Federal law prioritizes family preservation through prevention and support services.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that the department must make reasonable efforts to reunify before seeking termination, that a judge may weigh a failure of those efforts in deciding whether unfitness is merely temporary, but that a reasonable-efforts failure does not preclude an order in the child's best interest; it affirmed termination and left future visitation to the adoptive parents.
key_cases.relevance: The reasonable-efforts duty attaches to the voluntary service plan stage and is the yardstick for whether the agency did enough short of court action.
key_cases.quote: Before seeking to terminate parental rights, the department must make “reasonable efforts” aimed at restoring the child to the care of the natural parents.

key_cases.case_name: C.M. v. Commissioner of the Department of Children and Families
key_cases.holding: The Appeals Court held that DCF workers have absolute immunity for deciding to initiate care and protection proceedings and for their testimony, but only qualified immunity for their investigations and for factual assertions sworn on personal knowledge in an affidavit supporting a removal petition; it vacated summary judgment on the § 1983 claim based on the allegedly false affidavit.
key_cases.relevance: C.M. holds that DCF's authority is bounded by G. L. c. 119, §§ 24-29, and that a voluntary safety plan cannot itself create a basis for later action.
key_cases.quote: In sum, DCF workers are protected by absolute immunity in their decisions to initiate care and protection proceedings and in testifying at the subsequent hearings or trials on the petitions.

key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed termination, holding that the department discharged its duty to strengthen and encourage the family unit where it worked diligently without success and the additional services the mother sought would not have solved her chronic problems, and that a court appointed special advocate appointed as guardian ad litem may testify and submit a report.
key_cases.relevance: Georgia holds that the duty to strengthen the family is satisfied by diligent effort, not by provision of every service a parent requests.
key_cases.quote: Mary’s argument that the department failed to fulfil its duty to strengthen and encourage the family unit lacks merit.

key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed the judgment dispensing with the parents' consent to adoption, holding that a proceeding to terminate parental rights is not a "service, program, or activity" so the Americans with Disabilities Act may not be raised as a defense to it, while holding that the ADA, Massachusetts antidiscrimination law and the State Constitution do require the department to accommodate a disabled parent's special needs in the services it provides beforehand, and that the department did so here.
key_cases.relevance: Gregory measures the front-end service package against the department's duty to accommodate a parent's cognitive disability before any court action is sought.
key_cases.quote: the ADA, as well as Massachusetts anti-discrimination laws, regulations, and our Constitution all require the department to accommodate the parents' special needs in its provision of services

key_cases.case_name: Petition of Dept. of Public Welfare
key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed two Probate Court decrees dispensing with parental consent to the adoption of two children, holding that the judge applied the correct statutory standard and based the decrees on a proper assessment of all the relevant facts, while agreeing that the State must make every effort to strengthen and encourage family life before it moves to sever family ties permanently.
key_cases.relevance: This is the original Massachusetts statement of the duty to strengthen and encourage family life, the obligation a voluntary service plan is meant to discharge.
key_cases.quote: we agree that the State is required to make every effort to strengthen and encourage family life before it may proceed with plans to sever family ties permanently

key_cases.case_name: In Re the Department of Public Welfare to Dispense With Consent to Adoption
key_cases.holding: The SJC reversed a judgment dispensing with a mother's consent to the adoption of her child and remanded for further proceedings, holding that the judgment was unsupported by adequate findings as to the fitness of the surviving parent and emphasizing the recognized developmental risks that disruption of the parent-child relationship carries.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion grounds the department's duty to strengthen and encourage families in the demonstrated developmental harm that separation itself inflicts on a child.
key_cases.quote: there exists a "substantial and impressive consensus" among experts in the field of child development that "disruption of the parent-child relationship carries significant risks" for the child

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Emergency order transferring custody (DCF must file the care and protection petition on the next court day after taking emergency custody, M.G.L. c. 119, § 51B(c))
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An emergency order transfers custody for up to 72 hours only; custody continues past 72 hours solely if the court so determines after notice to the parents, guardian or custodian (M.G.L. c. 119, § 24)

timeline_requirements.deadline: 45 days for the department or agency to provide a copy of the service or case plan to the parent, guardian or custodian and to the attorneys for all parties appearing in the proceeding
timeline_requirements.starts_from: The department or agency filing an appearance in the proceeding (M.G.L. c. 119, § 29)

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Appointment of counsel for indigent parent
timeline_requirements.deadline: 14 days for the juvenile court and probate and family court departments, under procedures they must establish, to appoint counsel for an indigent parent, guardian or custodian
timeline_requirements.starts_from: A licensed child placement agency filing or appearing as a party in the action (M.G.L. c. 119, § 29)
